headlines.article_text: Oil prices today: Brent, WTI fall Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Oil fell as traders weighed an unexpected increase in U.S. crude inventories against worries over supply disruptions after an Iran-backed attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. U.S. crude oil, gasoline and distillate inventories all rose last week, according to Reuters. The U.S. war with Iran has cost the Pentagon an estimated $38.1 billion through Aug. 1. In this article @CL.1 @LCO.1 @LCO26X Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Numerous merchant ships belonging to Iran and other countries remain at anchor in the Strait of Hormuz in Bandar Abbas, Iran, on Sept. 8, 2026. Fatemeh Bahrami | Anadolu | Getty Images Oil retreated Wednesday after a report said U.S. energy inventories rose last week, with investors assessing the latest developments in Middle East conflict and associated supply risks. Futures for international benchmark Brent crude for November delivery dropped 1.02% to $107.64 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for October declined 1.29% to $104.46 per barrel. Brent U.S. crude oil, gasoline and distillate inventories all rose last week, Reuters reported, citing sources for data from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude inventories rose by 7.1 million barrels in the week ended Sept. 11, compared with analysts' expectations for a draw of about 1.6 million barrels, Reuters reported. Meanwhile, traders remain glued to developments in the Middle East, amid concerns over supply disruptions following an attack by Iran on Saudi Arabia's crucial East-West pipeline that led to its closure over the weekend. U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC in an interview on Tuesday that the closure was a brief interruption that will last days. Andy Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates, said in a note on Monday that "judging from the on-line pictures , it will take months to repair." The financial cost of the Middle East conflict is also being closely watched. According to a report released Tuesday by the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office, the U.S. war with Iran has cost the Pentagon an estimated $38.1 billion through Aug. 1 and could lead to another $2 billion to $3 billion being spent for each additional month of fighting. "Looking ahead, crude is likely to remain closely tied to security conditions along Gulf export routes and the pace of repairs to Saudi infrastructure," said Joseph Dahrieh, managing director at brokerage Tickmill. "Any further disruption to maritime flows or a prolonged pipeline outage could tighten the physical market and extend the advance in prices," Dahrieh added. CFO Peter Oey told CNBC that consumer lending is the “next frontier” for Grab as the company expands its financial services business. Photographer: Bryan van der Beek/Bloomberg via Getty Images Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images Grab is buying Singapore-based buy-now, pay-later platform Atome Financial as it looks to expand in consumer lending. The company announced it would acquire an initial 60% controlling stake in Atome for $1.49 billion in cash, with plans to buy the remaining 40% roughly two years after the first transaction closes. The two-stage structure was partly designed to "de-risk" the transaction from a capital allocation perspective, CFO Peter Oey told CNBC's " Squawk Box Asia " on Wednesday. watch now VIDEO 3:22 03:22 Grab CFO: Atome deal will help us leapfrog in consumer lending Squawk Box Asia Grab shares closed 3.64% lower on Nasdaq following the announcement. The acquisition is part of Grab's push to scale its financial services business beyond its existing offerings, with the company betting that Atome can help expand its reach in consumer lending. "All this together actually brings our capability to the next level when it comes to financial services," Oey, adding that the deal would be accretive to the business and contributed to Grab raising its 2028 outlook. Atome works with brands across travel, beauty and e-commerce, giving Grab access to areas where it has a more limited presence, Oey said. The transaction is expected to close next year, meaning Atome's contribution will be more meaningful toward the latter part of that year and into 2028, he said. Grab expects its financial services segment to generate $500 million in adjusted EBITDA by 2028. Grab plans to retain Atome's management team, while the period between the two stages will give the companies time to work on potential synergies, Oey said. Beyond the Atome deal, Oey pointed to micro-investing as another potential opportunity in Southeast Asia.
